title: The Heilbronner Weg Hut Chain, Allgäu High Route

bestPeriod.note: Snow can sit in the Bockkarscharte and on the shaded ledges of the Heilbronner Weg into early July; the traverse is safest from mid-July.

summary: A seven-day Allgäu hut chain from Kemptner Hütte over the secured Heilbronner Weg to Waltenbergerhaus, with a Prinz-Luitpold-Haus finale above Bad Hindelang.
hook: Oberstdorf sits at the foot of a limestone wall that the DAV's Heilbronn section wired for foot traffic in 1899, and the result is still one of the great secured ridge walks in the Northern Alps. This week climbs from the Trettach valley to Kemptner Hütte, crosses the Bockkarscharte to Rappenseehütte, edges along cable and ladder above 2,300 m to Waltenbergerhaus, and finishes with a lower-key hut night at Prinz-Luitpold-Haus above Bad Hindelang. Helmets on for one long day; quiet forest and alp meadow for the rest.

snapshot.Base(s): Oberstdorf, with a two-night extension to Hinterstein / Bad Hindelang
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 70-80 km, 4,600-5,200 m combined ascent; limestone ridge, scree, secured ledges (DAV blue/black), alpine meadow
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Memmingen (FMM) or Munich (MUC), train/bus to Oberstdorf; regional trains run direct from Munich Hbf in about 2h15
snapshot.Who It Suits: Fit hut-to-hut walkers who are comfortable with a cable-and-ladder day and carry their own gear between huts

itinerary.title: Into the Trettach valley
itinerary.morning: Arrive Oberstdorf, register at the tourist office for the Gästekarte (covers regional buses), and take the Oberallgäu bus to Spielmannsau, the road-end hamlet in the Trettach valley.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the gravel forestry track and then a steepening path up through spruce to Kemptner Hütte (1,846 m), run by DAV Sektion Kempten. Check in, claim a bunk in the Matratzenlager, and confirm tomorrow's forecast with the hut warden.
itinerary.evening: Half-board dinner, Käsespätzle is the house standard, and an early night. The hut's solar system means lights-out is enforced around 22:00.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km, 720 m ascent, negligible descent. Grade T2 on forestry track, T3 on the final approach. Water at Spielmannsau and the hut only.

itinerary.title: Over the Bockkarscharte to Rappenseehütte
itinerary.morning: Leave early. The path climbs scree and firm rock steps to the Bockkarscharte (2,599 m), the high point of the week, with the Mädelegabel massif close on the right. Snow can bank up here into July, ask the Kemptner warden the evening before.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the far side on loose limestone debris, easing onto grass benches, to Rappenseehütte (2,091 m), DAV Sektion Allgäu-Immenstadt's flagship hut and one of the largest in the range.
itinerary.evening: The terrace looks straight down the Rappensee basin. Book ahead, this hut fills in August.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km, 850 m ascent, 630 m descent. Grade T3, exposed rock steps near the Scharte, no cables. Carry 1.5 L; nothing reliable between huts.

itinerary.title: The Heilbronner Weg
itinerary.morning: The signature day. From Rappenseehütte the trail contours below the Hohes Licht and Mädelegabel on a narrow, cable-secured ledge, the original 1899 Heilbronner Weg, with ladders and iron stemples across the steepest rock bands. Helmets on before the first cable.
itinerary.afternoon: The route eases past the Trettachspitze flank before dropping to Waltenbergerhaus (1,932 m), DAV Sektion Allgäu-Immenstadt's second hut in the group, tucked under the Höfats.
itinerary.evening: Compare notes with other hikers on the terrace, everyone talks about the same three ladder pitches. Dry socks matter tonight; feet get wet on the shaded scree gullies.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km, 400 m ascent, 550 m descent. Grade DAV black / T4, continuously exposed with fixed cable and ladders; via-ferrata set genuinely recommended, not optional bravado. No water on route.

itinerary.title: Down to Oberstdorf, valley reset
itinerary.morning: Descend from Waltenbergerhaus through the Bärgündeletal past the Rappenalpe to Einödsbach, then the flat valley road back into Oberstdorf. Legs get a rest; feet finally dry out.
itinerary.afternoon: Laundry, a swim at the Eduard-Thöny-Bad, and a resupply stop for the second half of the week.
itinerary.evening: Bus or short train hop toward Bad Hindelang for tomorrow's start; overnight in Oberstdorf if the connection is late.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km, negligible ascent, 900 m descent. Grade T1-T2, well-graded valley path throughout.

itinerary.title: Into the Bärgündeletal to Prinz-Luitpold-Haus
itinerary.morning: Bus to Hinterstein, then on to Giebelhaus, the road-end for the Bärgündeletal on this side of the range. The trail climbs steadily through larch and open alp.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach Prinz-Luitpold-Haus (1,846 m), DAV Sektion Allgäu-Immenstadt's hut below the Rauhhorn, with the Hochvogel massif filling the skyline south.
itinerary.evening: This hut has a working still and makes its own Enzian, one glass, not two, before a big day tomorrow.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km, 950 m ascent, negligible descent. Grade T2, wide alp path, no exposure.

itinerary.title: The Schrecksee balcony
itinerary.morning: Day walk without full packs: contour east from the hut to the Schrecksee, a turquoise tarn below the Rotspitze that is, deservedly, one of the most photographed lakes in the Allgäu.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop back via the Willersalpe, a working dairy alp that sells Bergkäse and buttermilk in season, then return to the hut for a second night.
itinerary.evening: Sunset over the Hochvogel from the terrace; this is the pay-off day.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km, 550 m ascent, 550 m descent. Grade T2-T3, rocky in short sections near the lake outlet.

itinerary.title: Descent and departure
itinerary.morning: Descend the Bärgündeletal to Giebelhaus, retracing Day 5's line down through the larches.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus to Bad Hindelang or Hinterstein, connect to Sonthofen for the onward train, or back to Oberstdorf for a final Allgäu lunch.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km, negligible ascent, 950 m descent. Grade T1-T2.

accommodationStrategy.name: Haus Trettachtal
accommodationStrategy.description: A short walk from the Spielmannsau bus stop, with a boot room and drying cupboard that matters after the Heilbronner Weg. Good for the two nights bracketing the ridge traverse.

accommodationStrategy.name: Kemptner Hütte / Rappenseehütte / Waltenbergerhaus / Prinz-Luitpold-Haus
accommodationStrategy.description: All four are DAV member huts with staffed kitchens and half-board service. Book each directly through the hut's own online reservation form (linked from alpenverein.de) or by phone; popular August weekends fill three to four months out, and DAV members get priority and a lower Hüttennachtlager rate.

accommodationStrategy.name: Gasthof in Bad Hindelang or Hinterstein
accommodationStrategy.description: A traditional Allgäu guesthouse near the Giebelhaus bus stop, useful as a base for the Prinz-Luitpold-Haus approach if you prefer not to stay two nights at the hut itself.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; Bavarian mountain rescue (Bergwacht Bayern) is best reached via 112, which routes directly to the alpine rescue coordination centre.
logistics.weather: Allgäu limestone builds afternoon convective storms from July onward; be off the Heilbronner Weg's exposed ledges by early afternoon.
logistics.bookingWindows: DAV huts on this route run genuine reservation systems, not just a phone that rings out, book Rappenseehütte and Waltenbergerhaus first, since they sell out earliest in July and August.

other.label: Hüttenschlafsack
other.text: A sleeping bag liner is mandatory in every DAV hut; duvets are provided but bare mattress contact is not allowed. Buy one in Oberstdorf if you arrive without.

other.label: Cash
other.text: Huts take cards increasingly often but connectivity is patchy; carry €80, €100 in cash for drinks, showers and Enzian.

other.label: Gästekarte
other.text: Oberstdorf and Bad Hindelang guest cards, issued at check-in, cover regional buses including the Spielmannsau and Giebelhaus lines, confirm validity dates with your host.

other.label: Waymarks
other.text: DAV blue markers denote the most demanding, exposure-graded routes (the Heilbronner Weg itself); black/red signage on approach paths corresponds to standard mountain trail, T2-T3.

proTips: Call Rappenseehütte the same week you book flights, it is the pinch point of the whole itinerary.
Ask the Kemptner Hütte warden about snow in the Bockkarscharte the evening before; conditions change week to week into July.
Walk the Heilbronner Weg west to east (Rappensee to Waltenberger), which puts the morning sun at your back on the exposed ledges rather than in your eyes.
Buy Bergkäse direct from the Willersalpe on Day 6, it does not travel to shops in the valley.
Carry earplugs; DAV dormitories are efficient but not soundproof in August.
The Schrecksee day (Day 6) works as a stand-alone add-on even without the full hut chain, worth remembering if weather forces a shorter week.
Reserve the Oberstdorf-Hinterstein bus connection in writing during peak season; the midday service is thin.

packingNotes: Via-ferrata set (harness plus two carabiners) for the Heilbronner Weg, several operators in Oberstdorf rent full kits.
Hüttenschlafsack, required at every hut on the route.
Sturdy boots with real ankle support; this is not a trail-shoe traverse.
1.5 L water capacity minimum; refill points are hut taps only above 1,800 m.
Headtorch for the early Day 2 start.
Cash in small notes for hut bars and the Willersalpe.
A lightweight down layer, Rappenseehütte and the Bockkarscharte are cold even in August mornings.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Old snow blocks the Bockkarscharte.** Fallback: descend to Spielmannsau instead and bus around to Rappenseehütte's lower approach from Oberstdorf, rejoining the route for Day 3.
**Storm builds over the Heilbronner Weg.** Fallback: wait it out at Rappenseehütte, the warden tracks conditions closely and will advise against starting rather than have hikers caught on the cables.
**Rappenseehütte fully booked.** Fallback: Kemptner Hütte to Waltenbergerhaus in one long day is feasible for strong parties, skipping the overnight, though it makes for a 9-hour day.
**Wet boots after Day 3's shaded gullies.** Fallback: every hut on this chain has a drying room; use it, and carry a spare pair of socks in a dry bag.
**Missed bus connection to Hinterstein.** Fallback: a taxi from Oberstdorf to Giebelhaus costs a fraction of a lost hut booking and keeps Day 5 on schedule.
